clue.text: In leaf where one starts to surf

parts.note: being in is being at home
a leaf of a book is a page

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a place inside a leaf where a surfer begins riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surf' looks like the sea, but it means browsing the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser's start-up website is the first page shown before a user begins browsing the web.

clue.text: Source of water making footwear squeak?

parts.note: hose means stockings or socks, worn on the feet
to pipe is to make a shrill, squeaky sound

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes shoes squeak, perhaps water in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden tube delivers water from the tap, so it is literally where the water comes out.

clue.text: Foul smell is located in US city mostly

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the contraction sitting within the shortened city
most of the word, so the city name loses its last letter

parts.note: Miami is a city in Florida
is can be contracted to 's

explanation.surface: A report that a bad odour hangs over most of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is shortened to the S of 's, and goes inside MIAM, which is Miami without its final I.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasm (variant of miasma) is a noxious vapour or unpleasant odour.

clue.text: Crowd around church is to wobble

indicators.note: the word for crowd goes round the other piece

parts.note: to crowd is to press
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A throng packed round a church makes the building wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: To precess is to undergo precession, the slow wobble of a spinning body's axis.

clue.text: Try to sell up, producing nervous response?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to plug a product is to promote it

explanation.surface: A salesman pushing hard and gulping nervously while doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PLUG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowing hard is a typical sign of nerves or apprehension, as when facing something frightening.

clue.text: Original border claimed by China?

indicators.note: the border is taken inside the friend, as territory is claimed

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for pal
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A frontier disputed with the Chinese state.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so a china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means first or earliest, belonging to the very beginning, which is what original also means.

clue.text: Kurosawa film overwhelms peculiar main Oscar winner

indicators.note: the film title surrounds and swamps the jumbled word

parts.note: Ran (1985) is Akira Kurosawa's epic version of King Lear

indicators.note: peculiar suggests the word main is put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A Japanese film eclipsing a strange main Academy Award winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain Man (1988) won the Academy Award for Best Picture, so it is an example of an Oscar-winning film.

clue.text: Guru: mother and Arab enthralled by his greeting

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: held captive inside, so the abbreviation sits within the possessive word

parts.note: taken as written
Ar. is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A mother and an Arab charmed by a guru's welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' looks like a mere possessive pointing at the guru, but it gives its own letters and holds the Arab abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual teacher, so the word means a guru.

clue.text: Heartless lady upset gent, penning first of cruel words

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word lady are removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: the turned title encloses a letter as if writing it inside
in a down clue upset turns the word for gent upside down

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman

indicators.note: only the opening letter of cruel is used

explanation.surface: A heartless woman upsets a man by writing him cruel words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SIR to RIS, and 'penning' puts C, the 'first of cruel', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the text of a song, the words set to its music.

clue.text: How to make gale stir into life?

parts.note: shaking up the letters of a leg rearranges them into the word gale

explanation.surface: A question about stirring up a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'shake A LEG', and its anagram makes GALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up or get moving, rousing oneself into action.

clue.text: What's long filling stomach on a man?

definitions.text: What's long filling stomach on a man?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
the abbreviation goes inside the word for stomach, filling it

parts.note: gut is the stomach
Tony is a man's name

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps a man's belly full for so long.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: the sin of keeping one's stomach endlessly filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is excessive eating, a habit of constantly stuffing oneself beyond need.

clue.text: One moves to forefront of singers, producing heavenly stuff

indicators.note: the letter for one is shifted to the front of the word for singers

parts.note: a choir is a body of singers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soloist steps forward from the choir to produce divine music.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods.

clue.text: Current measure blocking a treat

indicators.note: the unit sits inside, blocking the middle of the other word

parts.note: per means a, as in a pound a head
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: An electrician's gauge obstructs someone's treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not a link word: it is PER, as in 'ten pounds a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to indulge or spoil them, which is to treat them.

clue.text: Corporation engaging right fellow to provide spice

indicators.note: the belly word takes in the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A company hiring the right man to supply its spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is not a business here but a humorous old word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow powdered root used as a seasoning in curries.

clue.text: Powerful cat nipping one soldier

indicators.note: the cat word grips the numeral inside it, as if nipping it

parts.note: puss is a cat
I is the Roman numeral one
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A strong cat biting a lone soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Puissant is a literary word for mighty or potent, from Old French.

clue.text: Reports urge economy by Society

indicators.note: by means set alongside, here placed after

parts.note: to press is to urge
a cutting back is an economy

explanation.surface: Reports pressing a society to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: These are articles clipped from newspapers, so they are reports kept on file.

clue.text: Chef with food that is eaten by the Queen

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation consumes the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
scoff is slang for food
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cook with a dish devoured by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Escoffier was the celebrated French cook who codified classic French cuisine.

clue.text: Wary accepting battered hat of durable material

indicators.note: the word for wary takes the jumbled piece inside

parts.note: leery means wary or suspicious

indicators.note: battered suggests the word hat is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A cautious person accepts a battered but tough hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' signals the anagram of the three-letter headwear, giving ATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery describes something tough like hide, resembling tanned animal skin.

clue.text: Susceptible to changes in character, affecting key events?

definitions.meaning: said of text matching that treats capitals and small letters differently
humorously, sensitive to the important cases, as in a court's key cases

explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a typed letter, whose case is upper or lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that distinguishes capital from lower-case letters is described with this term.

clue.text: Problem turning up among regular payments from non-central areas

indicators.note: the reversed word sits among, inside, the payments

parts.note: subs are subscriptions, paid regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom

parts.note: a rub is a problem, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: A snag arising in subscriptions from outlying districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives BUR; 'regular payments' is a single synonym, not a letter selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbs are the residential districts away from a city's centre.

clue.text: I remain in possession of politician's expenses payment

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the politician inside, possessing him

parts.note: to rest is to remain
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone retaining a politician's expenses claim.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is an advance of money to an agent or employee for official expenditure.

clue.text: Wild behaviour involving unknown trips in planes?

indicators.note: the word for wild behaviour wraps round the unknown

parts.note: a fling is a spell of wild or self-indulgent behaviour
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Wild behaviour involving mysterious flights.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by air is the activity of journeys made aboard aircraft.

clue.text: Rescue service's boost, carrying last of antidote (snake)

indicators.note: the boost word carries the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a lift is a boost

indicators.note: only the final letter of antidote is taken

parts.note: a boa is a snake

explanation.surface: A rescue team carries the antidote for a snake bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat launched to save people at sea, run in Britain by the RNLI charity.

clue.text: Toper throttling glutton for source of booze?

indicators.note: the drinker's word grips the glutton round the middle

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a toper
a pig is a glutton

explanation.surface: A drunk strangling a greedy guzzler over the drink supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a tap on a cask, from which beer or wine flows.

clue.text: Extend length to show aggression

parts.note: to grow is to extend or get larger

explanation.surface: Stretching out to make oneself look threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog snarls with a low throaty noise when it is hostile or threatening.

clue.text: German guy in gambling game, losing head

indicators.note: the first letter of the gambling game is dropped

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance

explanation.surface: A German man at a betting game, losing his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, as in Otto von Bismarck.

clue.text: I run to secure French company, adopting extra formality

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the company fast inside them

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Cie is compagnie, the French for company

explanation.surface: A businessman racing to secure a French firm and becoming more formal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler in manner, more frosty and stiffly formal, is what icier means of behaviour.

clue.text: Lead and tin-ware shipping fluid litre?

indicators.note: the tinware takes the jumbled word aboard, inside it

parts.note: tole is lacquered or painted tinware

indicators.note: fluid means the letters of litre are fluid, not fixed

explanation.surface: Lead and tin goods carrying a litre of fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is not the metal but a leading part; 'fluid' rearranges LITRE to ITLER.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the character the play is named after is often the star or lead role.

clue.text: Dressing heartlessly in bright colours

indicators.note: the central letter of the dressing word is cut out

parts.note: a garnish is a dressing for food

explanation.surface: Dressing in loud colours without any heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish describes things that are showy and lurid, gaudy to the eye.

clue.text: Two railroads running behind Army pub

indicators.note: the two railway abbreviations follow the army word

parts.note: a host is an army
EL is an elevated railroad in the US; RY is short for railway
EL is an elevated railroad in the US; RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: Two railways running behind an army's pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn or tavern, an old word for a public house.
